title: MEHMO SYNDROME
alt_titles: MENTAL RETARDATION, EPILEPTIC SEIZURES, HYPOGONADISM AND HYPOGENITALISM, MICROCEPHALY, AND OBESITY
MENTAL RETARDATION, X-LINKED, SYNDROMIC, BORCK TYPE

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that MEHMO syndrome (MEHMO) is caused by hemizygous mutation in the EIF2S3 gene (300161) on chromosome Xp22.11.

checks.claim: MEHMO syndrome is caused by hemizygous mutation in the EIF2S3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequence analysis indicated that all patients carried a hemizygous mutation in EIF2S3 located on chromosome X as the most likely disease-relevant change.
checks.explanation: The paper links MEHMO syndrome to hemizygous EIF2S3 mutations.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 gene is located on chromosome Xp22.11.
checks.evidence_quote: a candidate region spanning 10.7 megabases on the short arm of the X chromosome (Xp22.11-p21.1; Figure S2A)
checks.explanation: EIF2S3 falls in the Xp22.11-p21.1 linkage region. The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: MEHMO syndrome is an X-linked recessive intellectual developmental disorder in males (Skopkova et al., 2017). Steinmuller et al. (1998) named it after its main features: mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity. Affected males have severe developmental delay (Delozier-Blanchet et al., 1989), and many die early in childhood (Skopkova et al., 2017). Skopkova et al. (2017) reported that some patients also have glucose dysregulation and pituitary hormone deficiencies.

checks.claim: MEHMO syndrome is an X-linked recessive intellectual developmental disorder in males.
checks.evidence_quote: Syndrome * | MEHMO (MIM# 300148), syndromic XLID | CACH/VWM (MIM# 603896) | Syndromic ID with diabetes (MIM# 616817) | WRS (MIM# 226980) | MEDS (MIM# 614231) | WFS (MIM# 222300) | ACPHD (MIM# 616192) | MSS (MIM# 248800) Inheritance | X-linked recessive
checks.explanation: Table 3 lists MEHMO as syndromic XLID with X-linked recessive inheritance. The affected individuals described are males.

checks.claim: Steinmuller et al. (1998) named MEHMO syndrome after its main features: mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity.
checks.evidence_quote: Based on the major clinical symptoms this condition is referred to by the acronym MEHMO.
checks.explanation: The title spells out the acronym: mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and -genitalism, microcephaly, obesity.

checks.claim: Males affected with MEHMO syndrome have severe developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: Two brothers are described with a severe syndrome of postnatal growth and mental retardation which includes extreme microcephaly, obesity developing during infancy, microgonadismsm, and a characteristic amphora-shaped facies.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes two affected brothers with severe postnatal growth and mental retardation. It also says their mental retardation was much more severe than in BFL syndrome. This matches the claim of severe developmental delay in affected males. The paper does not use the name MEHMO; the draft applies that name to this family.

checks.claim: Many males affected with MEHMO syndrome die early in childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: Life span | Few months, oldest patient alive at 18 y
checks.explanation: Table 3 gives a life span of a few months. Table 1 records deaths at 2 years, 7 months, 2 months and 10 months (family 3) and at 12 months (family 7).

checks.claim: Some patients with MEHMO syndrome have glucose dysregulation.
checks.evidence_quote: Moreover, three of the patients developed insulin-dependent diabetes in the first year of life.
checks.explanation: The paper also reports neonatal hypoglycemia (Table 1).

checks.claim: Some patients with MEHMO syndrome have pituitary hormone deficiencies.
checks.evidence_quote: Other Endocrinopathy | Panhypopituitarism | Partial hypopituitarism | Small thyroid (1/4) | − | Low GH levels (2/3)
checks.explanation: Table 1 reports panhypopituitarism, partial hypopituitarism and low growth hormone levels in some patients.

paragraphs.text: Steinmuller et al. (1998) described a large three-generation family with an X-chromosomal mental retardation syndrome. Its clinical hallmarks were mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity, and they named the condition with the acronym MEHMO. Life expectancy of patients was less than 2 years.

checks.evidence_quote: A previously unrecognised X-chromosomal mental retardation syndrome is described.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the syndrome and says the linkage analysis was done in a large three-generation family.

checks.claim: The clinical hallmarks of the syndrome in the Steinmuller et al. (1998) family were mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity.
checks.evidence_quote: Clinical hallmarks are mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism, and -genitalism, microcephaly and obesity.
checks.explanation: The hallmarks match the claim.

checks.claim: Steinmuller et al. (1998) named the condition with the acronym MEHMO.
checks.evidence_quote: Based on the major clinical symptoms this condition is referred to by the acronym MEHMO.
checks.explanation: The abstract names the condition MEHMO.

checks.claim: Life expectancy of patients with MEHMO in the Steinmuller et al. (1998) family was less than 2 years.
checks.evidence_quote: Life expectancy of patients is less than two years.
checks.explanation: The life expectancy matches the claim.

paragraphs.text: Borck et al. (2012) reported a family in which males had X-linked syndromic intellectual disability with microcephaly, among other features.

checks.evidence_quote: three male individuals were affected by an intellectual disability (ID) syndrome with apparent X-chromosomal inheritance (X-linked ID, XLID)
checks.explanation: The paper describes a family with three affected males who have an X-linked intellectual disability syndrome that includes other features.

checks.claim: Affected males in the family reported by Borck et al. (2012) had microcephaly.
checks.evidence_quote: Clinical features included moderate-to-severe ID, microcephaly, short stature, and facial dysmorphic features
checks.explanation: Microcephaly is listed among the shared clinical features.

paragraphs.text: Steinmuller et al. (1998) described MEHMO as an X-chromosomal mental retardation syndrome. Skopkova et al. (2017) gave the inheritance of MEHMO syndrome as X-linked recessive.

paragraphs.text: Steinmuller et al. (1998) used haplotype and two-point linkage analyses in a large three-generation family to assign the MEHMO locus to Xp21.1-p22.13.

checks.claim: Steinmuller et al. (1998) used haplotype and two-point linkage analyses in a large three-generation family with MEHMO.
checks.evidence_quote: Haplotype and two-point linkage analyses in a large three-generation family assign the disease locus to Xp21.1-p22.13
checks.explanation: The methods and the family match the claim.

checks.claim: Steinmuller et al. (1998) assigned the MEHMO locus to Xp21.1-p22.13.
checks.evidence_quote: assign the disease locus to Xp21.1-p22.13, to a region that is flanked by CYBB and DXS365.
checks.explanation: The locus matches the claim.

paragraphs.text: In affected males of a family with X-linked syndromic intellectual disability, Borck et al. (2012) found a hemizygous missense mutation, c.665T-C (ile222-to-thr, I222T), in the EIF2S3 gene. EIF2S3 encodes eIF2-gamma, the core subunit of the heterotrimeric eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 (eIF2) complex. In human cells, the I222T mutation disrupted eIF2 complex formation by specifically impairing the binding of eIF2-beta to eIF2-gamma. In yeast, the analogous mutation in eIF2-gamma also impaired eIF2-beta binding. Borck et al. (2012) concluded that the yeast Val281 mutations, and by analogy the human I222T mutation, impair eIF2 complex integrity and lead to defects in translation initiation.

checks.claim: Borck et al. (2012) studied affected males of a family with X-linked syndromic intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: three male individuals were affected by an intellectual disability (ID) syndrome with apparent X-chromosomal inheritance (X-linked ID, XLID)
checks.explanation: The paper studied affected males from one family with X-linked intellectual disability.

checks.claim: Borck et al. (2012) found a missense mutation, c.665T-C (I222T), in the EIF2S3 gene in affected males of a family with X-linked syndromic intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: Capillary sequencing confirmed the c.665T>C (p.Ile222>Thr) mutation (Figure 1C) and showed that it cosegregated with the ID syndrome in the family.
checks.explanation: The variant and protein change match the paper.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 I222T mutation was hemizygous in the affected males reported by Borck et al. (2012).
checks.evidence_quote: Identification of a hemizygous EIF2S3 missense variant c.665T>C (p.Ile222Thr).
checks.explanation: The figure legend states the variant is hemizygous.

checks.claim: EIF2S3 encodes eIF2-gamma, the core subunit of the heterotrimeric eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 (eIF2) complex.
checks.evidence_quote: a missense mutation in eIF2γ (encoded by EIF2S3), the core subunit of the heterotrimeric eIF2 complex
checks.explanation: The paper says EIF2S3 encodes eIF2-gamma, the core subunit of the eIF2 complex.

checks.claim: In human cells, the EIF2S3 I222T mutation disrupted eIF2 complex formation by specifically impairing the binding of eIF2-beta to eIF2-gamma.
checks.evidence_quote: the I222T mutation identified in the affected individuals disrupts eIF2 complex formation by specifically impairing the binding of eIF2β to human eIF2γ.
checks.explanation: This is shown in HeLa cells.

checks.claim: In yeast, the mutation in eIF2-gamma analogous to human EIF2S3 I222T impaired eIF2-beta binding.
checks.evidence_quote: In contrast, the eIF2γ-V281T mutation substantially impaired eIF2β binding (Figure 2D, lanes 5–6)
checks.explanation: V281T in yeast is the analogous mutation, and it impaired eIF2-beta binding.

checks.claim: Borck et al. (2012) concluded that the yeast eIF2-gamma Val281 mutations, and by analogy the human EIF2S3 I222T mutation, impair eIF2 complex integrity and lead to defects in translation initiation.
checks.evidence_quote: we conclude that the Val281 mutations in yeast eIF2γ, and by analogy the I222T mutation in human eIF2γ, impair eIF2 complex integrity leading to defects in translation initiation
checks.explanation: The paper states this conclusion directly.

paragraphs.text: Moortgat et al. (2016) identified a hemizygous frameshift mutation in the EIF2S3 gene, c.1394_1397del (p.Ile465SerfsTer4), in affected patients.

checks.claim: Moortgat et al. (2016) identified a frameshift mutation in the EIF2S3 gene, c.1394_1397del (p.Ile465SerfsTer4), in affected patients.
checks.evidence_quote: a frameshift mutation (c.1394_1397del p.(Ile465Serfs*4)) were identified in the EIF2S3 gene in the hemizygous state in affected patients
checks.explanation: The abstract names this frameshift mutation in EIF2S3 in affected patients. p.Ile465SerfsTer4 is the same variant as p.(Ile465Serfs*4), written in a different notation.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 c.1394_1397del mutation was hemizygous in the affected patients reported by Moortgat et al. (2016).
checks.evidence_quote: a frameshift mutation (c.1394_1397del p.(Ile465Serfs*4)) were identified in the EIF2S3 gene in the hemizygous state in affected patients
checks.explanation: The abstract says the mutation was hemizygous in affected patients.

paragraphs.text: In affected males of a family with X-linked syndromic intellectual disability and microcephaly, Borck et al. (2012) found a hemizygous c.665T-C transition in the EIF2S3 gene, resulting in an ile222-to-thr (I222T) substitution. In human HeLa cells, the I222T mutation impaired the binding of eIF2-beta to eIF2-gamma. In yeast, the analogous V281T mutation substantially impaired eIF2-beta binding. From the yeast Val281 mutations, Borck et al. (2012) inferred by analogy that I222T impairs eIF2 complex integrity and causes defects in translation initiation.

checks.claim: Borck et al. (2012) studied affected males of a family with X-linked syndromic intellectual disability and microcephaly.
checks.evidence_quote: Male family members affected by intellectual disability and microcephaly are shown as filled symbols
checks.explanation: The paper studied affected males with X-linked intellectual disability and microcephaly.

checks.claim: Borck et al. (2012) found a c.665T-C transition in the EIF2S3 gene, resulting in an ile222-to-thr (I222T) substitution, in affected males of a family with X-linked syndromic intellectual disability and microcephaly.
checks.evidence_quote: Capillary sequencing confirmed the c.665T>C (p.Ile222>Thr) mutation (Figure 1C) and showed that it cosegregated with the ID syndrome in the family.
checks.explanation: The variant matches the paper. T>C is a transition.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 c.665T-C (I222T) mutation was hemizygous in the affected males reported by Borck et al. (2012).
checks.evidence_quote: Identification of a hemizygous EIF2S3 missense variant c.665T>C (p.Ile222Thr).
checks.explanation: The figure legend states the variant is hemizygous.

checks.claim: In human HeLa cells, the EIF2S3 I222T mutation impaired the binding of eIF2-beta to eIF2-gamma.
checks.evidence_quote: Whereas eIF2α and eIF2β were co-precipitated with the tagged wild type eIF2γ on Ni2+ affinity resin (Figure 2E, lanes 3–4), substantially less eIF2β was pulled-down with eIF2γ-I222T
checks.explanation: The experiment was done in HeLa cells.

checks.claim: In yeast, the V281T mutation in eIF2-gamma, analogous to human EIF2S3 I222T, substantially impaired eIF2-beta binding.
checks.evidence_quote: In contrast, the eIF2γ-V281T mutation substantially impaired eIF2β binding (Figure 2D, lanes 5–6)
checks.explanation: The paper reports this directly.

checks.claim: From the yeast eIF2-gamma Val281 mutations, Borck et al. (2012) inferred by analogy that EIF2S3 I222T impairs eIF2 complex integrity and causes defects in translation initiation.
checks.evidence_quote: we conclude that the Val281 mutations in yeast eIF2γ, and by analogy the I222T mutation in human eIF2γ, impair eIF2 complex integrity leading to defects in translation initiation
checks.explanation: The paper states this inference by analogy directly.

paragraphs.text: Moortgat et al. (2016) identified a hemizygous 4-bp deletion (c.1394_1397del) in the EIF2S3 gene in affected patients. The deletion causes a frameshift, Ile465SerfsTer4.

checks.claim: Moortgat et al. (2016) identified a 4-bp deletion (c.1394_1397del) in the EIF2S3 gene in affected patients.
checks.evidence_quote: a frameshift mutation (c.1394_1397del p.(Ile465Serfs*4)) were identified in the EIF2S3 gene in the hemizygous state in affected patients
checks.explanation: The deletion c.1394_1397del covers nucleotides 1394 to 1397, which is 4 bp. The 4-bp size follows directly from this notation.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 c.1394_1397del deletion was hemizygous in the affected patients reported by Moortgat et al. (2016).
checks.evidence_quote: were identified in the EIF2S3 gene in the hemizygous state in affected patients
checks.explanation: The abstract says the deletion was hemizygous in affected patients.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 c.1394_1397del deletion causes a frameshift, Ile465SerfsTer4.
checks.evidence_quote: a frameshift mutation (c.1394_1397del p.(Ile465Serfs*4))
checks.explanation: The abstract calls the deletion a frameshift and gives its protein effect as p.(Ile465Serfs*4), the same as Ile465SerfsTer4.
